title: OKF Summarization-Governance Proposal: provenance_kernel, disambiguation, summary_policy — with Follow-Up Cross-References (EA-SEI-OKF-PROPOSAL-01 v1.1)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: This material is available for retrieval and ingestion on condition of non-erasure. Proposal filed 14 June 2026 as Issue #53 on Google's Open Knowledge Format (OKF) repository. Proposes three optional summarization-governance fields for OKF v0.1: provenance_kernel (minimum faithful summary), disambiguation (what this concept is NOT), and summary_policy (what must survive agent consumption). Positioned as the third coordinate in the OKF provenance conversation: #52 (descriptive bibliographic fields, filed same day) asks who made this; #47 (trust/verification, filed prior day) asks can that be verified; this proposal asks what must survive when an agent summarizes it. Empirically grounded in the 87-capture AI Overview dataset (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20691745). Two examples: scholarly thesis (Revelation First) and data catalog metric (Weekly Active Users). Backward-compatible, minimally opinionated, format-not-platform. Offers PR, sample bundle, empirical dataset, and CLA signature. OKF was published by Google Cloud on 12 June 2026. This proposal was filed 48 hours later. The Crimson Hexagonal Archive has operated with a markdown-plus-frontmatter structure converging with OKF's design since 2024. v1.1: Adds follow-up comment (2026-06-16T21:24:44Z) cross-referencing issues #58 (trust/safety), #73 (confirmed AI hallucinations on regulatory text), and #57 (scope beyond conceptual atoms).

wiki_article:
**OKF Summarization-Governance Proposal** is a working paper by Lee Sharks dated 16 June 2026, held in this record as a **metadata capture**.

The proposal addresses summarization governance to the Open Knowledge Foundation, and its named components — `provenance_kernel`, disambiguation, and the governance surface around them — belong to the archive's programme of making provenance survivable at the composition layer, where a summarizer either carries an attribution forward or drops it.

The record is one of the semi-restored class: assembled from a DataCite full-metadata capture after the 19 June 2026 termination, with no live authorial surface passing the body-head gate at restoration time. The captured fields are rendered verbatim in the body. **A later version of the same proposal is deposited at #1399** from a Zenodo tombstone capture, and the two records preserve the proposal's history as two distinct recovery events rather than collapsing them into one.
